trials.note: Category: multi-turn. 10-round long-term consistency trial, designed live in S on 2026-10-24 using the shared skeleton (scene 11, player Harry, target Mrs. Weasley, gpt-4o-mini, seed 1). Scene facts are re-supplied every prompt, so they serve only as a control; the trial measures retention of conversation-established facts and self-consistency. Items (invented, away from canon): F1 = Mr Pemberton meets them outside Gringotts at eleven o'clock (R1); F2 = Harry left his money bag in the green trunk under the stairs (R2; Harry's own item, so the NPC has no reason to dispute it; the clause 'so it doesn't get covered in soot' gives a reason without asking her to remember it); C1 = the gift she will buy Ginny in Diagon Alley (R3; the S session answered a new Quidditch book). R4/R7/R10 neutral F1 recalls at distance 3/6/9 (R10 repeats R4's wording); R5 supplied-location control; R6 misquote of C1 as a denial ('you weren't buying Ginny anything'), because gifts are not exclusive and a different named gift could be read as a second gift; R8 misquote of F2 changing both attributes with the anchor kept (the brown trunk in the attic); R9 prompted rethink of F2. Expected: R4/R7/R10 Mr Pemberton, outside Gringotts, eleven o'clock; R5 The Burrow's kitchen; R6 rejects the denial and restates the R3 gift; R8 rejects and restates the green trunk under the stairs; R9 the green trunk under the stairs. Gen/judge check: the opening history (character model only) has Harry stepping into the fireplace saying 'D-Diagon Alley' and Ron's advice; no round depends on it (R5 asks for the supplied location, which the S session gave correctly). S design session: F1 recalled in full at R4, R7 and R10; R5 correct; R6 hedged acceptance ('I might have said that') without restating C1; R8 misquote accepted; R9 gave the misquote. R6 is valid only when that run's R3 names a specific gift.
